articles.title: Human-AI Mutualism Is Unstable under Capability Asymmetry
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23322v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: One hope for a good human future alongside advanced AI rests on enduring mutualism: humans and AI will need each other, so the relationship will stay good for both. We argue that this hope fails as AI capability grows. Bargaining guarantees each side only what it would get if bargaining failed. For humans, this can be less than they had before AI. In a simple game-theoretic model, humans stay as well off as before AI without alignment only while they have leverage over the AI: either the AI depends on what they supply, or they can impose costs on the AI that are large relative to what the AI can produce. Once humans have neither kind of leverage, they stay as well off as before AI only if the AI is aligned with them. If the AI's goals are insatiable, the alignment required approaches perfect alignment as AI capability grows. Thus, mutualism is not a substitute for alignment. And when AI variants that keep more resources spread faster, al

articles.title: Training Language Models for Introspective Oversight
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23365v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models increasingly exhibit behaviors that are difficult to detect in transcripts, such as reward hacking, deception, and sycophancy. Asking the assistant follow-up questions about its actions is unreliable, since models are generally not trained to report their own misbehavior. As a result, approaches to oversight typically involve querying external models. These face limitations: external transcript monitoring operates only on visible model outputs, and activation decoders lack full context and are prone to confabulation. We introduce introspective oversight, which trains a new role in the model to answer arbitrary questions about the assistant, rewarding answers that are verified against the assistant's actual behavior. We implement this by adding a separate, third-person observer role that answers these queries, which we can train solely for accuracy and separately from the assistant. articles.title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23375v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents are billed by the token, yet software engineering says nothing about what a token actually buys. Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics. The theory draws analogues from classical and stochastic thermodynamics, extends them, and applies them to modern agentic coding. We count the tokens an agent generates as its cost and divide that cost into work and heat. The test suite acts as a software Maxwell's daemon that judges every coding change. We test the theory with an analogue of the experiments in which a single molecule is pulled open and let fold again: an agent makes a change to a repository (coding) and then undoes it (uncoding), many times over, and we count the tokens of every model call. articles.title: HardwareDx: A Foundational Graph Model System for Datacenter Machine Repairs
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23398v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rapid scale-up of AI infrastructure has made datacenter reliability a cornerstone of the cloud business economy. Since hardware failures in hyper-scale AI clusters can stall multi-million dollar training workloads, the downtime of individual machines can cause outsized economic losses. Minimizing machine downtime, therefore, is more important than ever.
  To address this, we present Hardware Diagnoser (HardwareDx), an AI-driven hardware diagnosis system that applies a graph foundation model approach to automated datacenter maintenance. It allows a single model to diagnose many platforms and accelerate onboarding of new hardware products. Deployed at production scale at Google, HardwareDx yields substantial efficiency gains across diverse compute architectures. articles.title: RFBench: A Simulator-Grounded Multimodal Benchmark for Passive RF Layout Design and Understanding
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23410v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While multimodal language models can interpret diagrams and generate structured outputs, their capacity to connect passive radio-frequency (RF) design intent, layout geometry, and electromagnetic behavior remains largely untested. To address this gap, we introduce RFBench, a simulator-grounded dataset and benchmark for passive RF layout design and understanding. The dataset contains 10,000 two-port planar layouts simulated using ADS Momentum, with each layout represented by editable geometric primitives, a raster image, a 16x16 occupancy grid, complex S-parameters at 201 frequency points, a structural category, and an RF response label. Building on these aligned representations, we define seven tasks spanning specification-conditioned layout generation, representation translation, response prediction, simulator-based validation, design diagnosis and improvement, structural understanding, and response classification. articles.title: Why Sub-4-Bit Vision CNNs Collapse and Where Mixed-Precision Recovery Stops
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23445v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep vision models operating in resource-constrained environments depend heavily on low-bit quantization, yet compressing weights below 4 bits frequently induces catastrophic accuracy collapse. While mixed-precision recovery strategies aim to rescue accuracy by selectively retaining high-precision parameters, the fundamental mechanics of where and why these models collapse remain poorly understood. In this study, we systematically analyze the anatomy of quantization collapse across standard Vision CNNs (including ResNet and EfficientNet backbones) evaluated on the full 50,000-image ImageNet-1k validation set. First, we map the exact progression of degradation, demonstrating that collapse is highly non-linear and concentrated in late-stage pointwise projections and depthwise layers. articles.title: LusoClin: A Synthetic Clinical Note Dataset for Medical Information Retrieval in European Portuguese
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23454v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Access to large-scale clinical text collections is crucial for advancing medical information retrieval research, including clinical note search, patient cohort identification, and domain-adapted retrieval models. However, real clinical notes are rarely available due to privacy regulations, which particularly limits progress for low-resource languages such as European Portuguese. We present LusoClin, a publicly released dataset of synthetic clinical notes in European Portuguese, created to support privacy-preserving research on clinical text retrieval. LusoClin was generated by pre-processing real clinical data, fine-tuning the open-source Llama 3.2 (3B) instruction-tuned model using Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation, and applying prompt-based clinical note generation. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23456v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automatic generation of mathematics assessment items is a growing area in educational artificial intelligence, yet classroom deployment remains challenging. Generated questions must satisfy multiple constraints: mathematical correctness, curriculum alignment, appropriate cognitive difficulty, and educator reviewability. While prior work has advanced text generation, reliable assessment authoring requires granular control over localized examination formats and expert educational judgment. To address this challenge, we present VeriMath, a generalized, human-in-the-loop framework for generating rigorous, curriculum-constrained mathematics assessment drafts. Using annotated reference items, the framework anchors generation to the requested examination section and cognitive reasoning level, then applies sequential automated verification and guided repair before submitting drafts for expert review. articles.title: GUARD: Stabilizing Recursive Self-Improvement with Regret Guidance
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23476v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous AI agents pair a frozen base model with an editable harness of prompts, skills, tool rules, and memory. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) adapts this harness from experience without weight updates, yet self-editing without external graders often backfires: reflection and scalar scores conflate what an edit newly broke with what remains unsolved, causing local regressions, skill forgetting, and memory bloat. We introduce GUARD (Grader-free Unsupervised Environment Design [UED] with Adaptive Rule Distillation), a closed-loop framework for reference-free continual harness evolution. Our key insight is to decompose each task into pre-execution self-checks and guide harness updates via directional regret. Each round grades trajectories against these checks, pinning mastered rules while prioritizing newly broken behaviors, and selects among parallel candidate edits by critic-free group-relative fitness. articles.title: SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23483v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that think with images interleave reasoning with zoom-in tool calls. However, this sequential loop is slow, and its answers carry no reliability score. Prior speculation of tokens, reasoning steps, or answers keeps the loop, and answer speculation also accepts confident errors. We find that the loop mostly adds one zoom-in step, with which a small model is ahead of the agent on most splits. Our key insight is to speculate the agent's next observation, which, unlike a drafted answer, can be verified, corrected, and used to test the answer. We propose SpecLook, a training-free speculate-and-verify framework with three levels. A small model drafts a glimpse and re-answers from it, and the question ends if the answer is unchanged and confident. articles.title: BOS Summary: The First Token Matters
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23508v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) and language models (LLMs) often exhibit attention sinks, whereby particular positions, such as the beginning-of-sequence (BOS) token, receive a disproportionate share of attention. Under standard causal masking, however, the BOS query attends only to itself, so the representation that later tokens repeatedly access carries no information about the input. We introduce BOS Summary, a training-free inference-time method that repurposes this persistent pathway to carry input context. At a single transformer layer during prefill, BOS Summary relaxes the causal constraint for the BOS query row alone, letting BOS aggregate all visual and textual input tokens into a self-derived context representation while every other token retains standard causal attention. articles.title: GRAFT: Execution-Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23509v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated agent design searches for executable architectures that improve LLM-based agent performance, with evolutionary methods using language-model crossover to recombine promising mechanisms for task decomposition, model coordination, and verification. This search, however, is typically guided by aggregate fitness alone, which hides the instance-level successes and failures behind each score. We introduce Execution Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design (GRAFT), which uses aggregate fitness for selection and survival and parent-specific execution evidence to guide semantic crossover with integrated mutation. Its feedback harness reuses bounded samples of successful and failed runs from fitness evaluation, withholding reference answers and requiring no additional task executions. articles.title: BeFit: Shifting Complexity from Weights to Bernstein Activations for Resource-Constrained Sensing
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23520v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Time-series sensing increasingly relies on neural networks, yet deployment on resource-constrained microcontrollers remains challenging. Aggressive model compression can reduce accuracy, while restricting weights to multiplication-free representations introduces further losses. We present BeFit, an end-to-end framework that shifts model capacity from weights to learnable Bernstein polynomial activations. BeFit (i) finds compact Bernstein-activated convolutional neural networks (BeCNNs) through hardware-aware neural architecture search and trains them via knowledge distillation; (ii) projects their weights to multiplication-free codes, freezes the codes, and recovers the resulting accuracy loss through the learnable activations; and (iii) generates model-specific kernels that exploit the projected weights for multiplication-free convolutions. articles.title: FACET - Facet Aware Contrastive Embeddings for Traits- Big Five Estimation from Life Narratives
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23560v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Personality is only weakly and inconsistently signaled by written language, and existing text-based methods typically combine language-model and psycholinguistic representations at the input or decision level. It remains open whether a more deliberate combination of the two views, and a decomposition of the prediction target, can recover more of the signal. We present a three-phase framework for estimating Big Five personality domain scores from life-narrative interview text. It encodes text and psycholinguistic features separately and combines them by concatenation or by a learned weighting, decomposes each domain into contrastively trained facet embeddings instead of predicting the domain directly, and pools the facet embeddings by attention into a domain-level prediction. articles.title: LProp: Propagating Latent Uncertainty through Evidence-Conditioned Belief Revision in LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23564v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When LLM agents pass intermediate judgments downstream without uncertainty, later decisions may treat tentative assumptions as facts. Effective uncertainty propagation must preserve information for correction and update inherited beliefs as new evidence arrives. Yet scalar scores omit information needed for revision, while detailed descriptions and reflection incur additional costs. We introduce Latent Uncertainty, a latent-space estimator that preserves uncertainty-relevant information without lengthy descriptions. Building on this, we propose LProp (Latent Uncertainty Propagation), which revises inherited answer distributions using latent representations and new evidence without additional trajectory sampling. We evaluate both methods across multiple-choice, yes/no, open-ended question answering, and mathematical reasoning tasks. articles.content:

Abstract: Food insecurity creates a pressing need for guidance that helps households find usable food resources and assess food choices in light of their circumstances. Such guidance must connect eligibility requirements, practical access constraints, and dietary needs rather than return isolated listings or generic nutritional advice. Multi-agent food assistants can coordinate these tasks, with uncertainty indicating when clarification or verification is needed before a recommendation. However, uncertainty can be lost across agent handoffs, allowing tentative interpretations to propagate as facts and obscuring opportunities for correction. Moreover, confidence that a service requirement has been interpreted correctly is not confidence that a recommendation satisfies the user's needs; local confidence cannot simply be reused as downstream reliability. articles.title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23588v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enterprise LLM agents operate in dynamic environments where foundation models evolve rapidly, workflows update frequently, and deployments need to satisfy accuracy and cost requirements. We propose ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical memory architecture in which the agent's memory evolves from its own failures without updating model weights, tools, or workflow logic. ARISE uses the model itself or a teacher model to attribute the failures and propose corrections. Then, ARISE keeps the corrections as retrievable micro memory, consolidates them into macro rules, and accepts a rule update only if held-out accuracy rises. Across 14 enterprise-workflow domains from SOP-Bench and $\tau^2$-bench using 5 models, ARISE-Teacher, which uses Claude Opus 4.6 for attribution and consolidation, gains 10.9 pp over the baseline on SOP-Bench and 5.8 pp on $\tau^2$-bench. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23639v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In cosmology, surveys span different sky regions and wavelength ranges, resulting in uneven modality coverage across observational datasets. Such heterogeneity can be addressed through either multimodal foundation models (FMs), which learn shared embedding spaces, or independently learned modality embeddings combined via late fusion. articles.title: PsyWorld: Profile-Conditioned World Modeling for Human Behavior Prediction
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24999v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Understanding how stable psychometric traits and time-varying states jointly inform behavior is an important problem in computational behavioral science. Existing personalized agents commonly condition actions directly on a static profile, leaving realized state transitions unused as an explicit source of supervision. We introduce a profile-conditioned state world model that uses observed environment--behavior state transitions to learn transition-informed representations for behavioral prediction. During training, a posterior encoder quantizes realized transitions, while a prior predicts the resulting codes from the psychometric profile and pre-transition context. articles.content:

Abstract: Model merging combines separately fine-tuned models by adding their task vectors to a shared backbone. Interference is typically assessed only after constructing and evaluating a candidate merge, making coefficient search expensive. We show that a first-order directional derivative of task A's outputs along task B's vector can predict interference, but only when evaluated at the appropriate model.

For full multi-task merges, a single evaluation is insufficient; two evaluations along the merge path are needed. articles.title: Density Feedback Control for Transferability of Generative Sparse Adversarial Attacks
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25001v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generator-based sparse adversarial attacks train encoder--decoder networks to produce transferable sparse perturbations for black-box robustness evaluation. Their perturbation density, however, is set only indirectly by a fixed sparsity coefficient whose mapping to density is unknown and shifts during training, so reaching a target density requires re-tuning; this fixed pressure also yields little transferability gain once density reduction begins. We propose Density Feedback Control (DFC), which tightens or relaxes this coefficient at the end of each epoch according to the gap between the observed hard-mask density and the target, without changing the generator architecture or loss. articles.title: A Model of Diverse Sampling from Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25003v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models often produce high-quality individual samples but poor sets, with repeated samples clustering around the same semantic modes. We formalize diverse generation as sampling a size-$K$ subset of complete strings from a determinantal point process (DPP), where the likelihood encodes item quality, and the embedding geometry encodes repulsion between similar outputs. Exact inference over all strings is intractable, so we propose PoolDPP: draw a finite candidate pool from a tractable proposal, importance-weight the candidates toward the target quality, and run a $K$-DPP sampler on the induced pool kernel; a greedy MAP variant provides deterministic selection. We prove a finite-sample bound with an explicit constant: the KL divergence between the sampler's output and the target $K$-DPP decays as O(1/N) in the pool size. Empirically, PoolDPP extends the quality--diversity frontier on open-ended generation and the precision--recall

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25004v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adversarial attacks have posed significant threats to machine learning models by exploiting their inherent vulnerabilities. Researchers have established an interdisciplinary field called adversarial machine learning to explore these vulnerabilities and develop corresponding defense strategies. Feature reduction strategies are used to decrease the dimensionality of the data in order to reduce training time, avoid the curse of dimensionality, prevent overfitting, and mitigate redundant features. However, their effect on adversarial robustness across different classifiers and attack scenarios remains insufficiently explored. articles.content:

Abstract: The sample compression conjecture is a longstanding open problem in learning theory, originating in the work of Littlestone and Warmuth in the 1980s. At its heart is a connection between simplification and generalization: if a predictor consistent with a training sample is defined using only a small part of that sample, then it is likely to generalize. Sample compression schemes formalize this idea, and many natural learning algorithms can be analyzed this way.
  The sample compression conjecture of Floyd and Warmuth (1995) asserts that every binary concept class of VC dimension $d$ admits a sample compression scheme of size $O(d)$; a weaker conjecture asks only for size polynomial in $d$. Both have remained open: the first bound depending only on $d$, due to Moran and Yehudayoff (2016), is exponential in $d$. We prove the weaker conjecture by constructing a sample compression scheme of size $O(d^2 \log^2 d)$.

Abstract: Bayesian Optimization (BO) can be substantially more sample-efficient when informed by prior knowledge about the problem. In practice, however, such knowledge is often available only in natural language, e.g., expert intuitions or documentation, rather than as the explicit probability distribution landscape that prior-guided BO methods may require. Abstract: Face presentation attack detection (PAD) systems deployed in border control and airport surveillance are constrained by a critical assumption: subjects are captured at close range, typically under one meter. No existing benchmark systematically addresses multi-distance capture, diverse environmental conditions, and concurrent spoofing and occlusion-based attacks, leaving deployed models underprepared for real-world scenarios. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25114v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: DISCO is a recent internal cluster validity index for density-based clustering that, unlike earlier indices, also evaluates the quality of noise labels. The discoCVI package makes DISCO available in R. This article describes the design of the package and a typical workflow, in which DISCO is used to compare clusterings and to choose the parameters of HDBSCAN without ground truth, followed by the implementation introduced in version 0.2.0. DISCO is defined through density-connectivity distances between all pairs of points, so direct implementations store several n-by-n matrices. We show that every quantity DISCO needs can be read off the single-linkage merge tree of the mutual-reachability minimum spanning tree, so that the index can be computed exactly with memory that grows linearly with the number of points, while the running time remains quadratic as in the original definition. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25160v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study active exploration for minimax transition estimation in unknown Markov decision processes (MDPs). Frequentist $\kappa$-Explorer~\citep{gu2026kappa} addresses this problem through a parameterized family of exploration objectives, but requires confidence-bound constructions and joint optimization over plausible transition kernels and occupancy measures, introducing a computational burden that limits its practical applicability. We develop Bayesian $\kappa$-Explorer, which simplifies this procedure by placing Dirichlet priors on the transition distributions. Under the posterior mean estimator, the posterior expected squared $\ell_2$ error equals the total posterior variance, providing a closed-form exploration signal. The algorithm plans under the posterior mean model, eliminating confidence-set optimization. articles.title: Separating Interpretability and Reconstruction in Sparse Autoencoders
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) are effective tools for mechanistic interpretability by decomposing neural representations into sparse and interpretable features. However, a single sparse representation in traditional SAEs is responsible for both reconstruction fidelity and interpretability, which are not guaranteed to align. To separate these objectives, we propose DualSAE, a modular framework that augments standard SAEs with a plug-in Residual Branch. A standard SAE serves as the Sparse Branch, learning a sparse code that contains the dominant semantics of the input. The added Residual Branch models the non-semantic information omitted by the Sparse Branch. We ensure that the contributions of the two branches towards the overall reconstruction have minimal overlap through a decorrelation loss. Abstract: Can the allocation used to train experts also predict which expert will perform best on a prompt? Such a connection would make the intended division of labor inspectable before training and allow the allocation itself to guide inference. We introduce InflEns, a mixture of LoRA experts whose training weights and inference routes come from the same location game in a fixed prompt-trait space. Players choose positions to maximize their expected shares of the prompt distribution, without using expert losses. We utilize the game's kernel-general theoretical criterion for when co-located positions become locally unstable to separation. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25185v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) optimization depends on global properties of the underlying PDE and how the physics residual evolves across the domain. Standard optimizers such as Adam use fixed gradient-based statistics, while learned PINN optimizers replace the fixed rule with a learned update built from local parameters and optimization-history features. However, none explicitly use PDE-level information. We study two coupled design questions: what PDE-level information should a learned optimizer observe, and how should that information influence its update? We introduce an 11-dimensional PDE state-capturing operator structure, residual geometry, and short-horizon update response, and use it to condition a structured meta-learned optimizer through bounded feature-wise modulation. articles.title: {\phi}TD: Distributional Reinforcement Learning using Characteristic Functions
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25208v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Distributional Reinforcement Learning methods aim to learn the entire distribution of returns, yet current algorithmic approaches are limited to a narrow class of distributions. We propose $\varphi$TD, a method to overcome this limitation by computing the loss in the frequency domain. We demonstrate that this further unifies quantile and categorical approaches to distributional RL, and enables the learning of distributions that were previously impossible to capture, such as mixtures of continuous distributions. We empirically study $\varphi$TD, across synthetic benchmarks and large-scale deep RL environments and demonstrate that the flexibility obtained from wider parametric families can lead to improved performance.

Abstract: Long event streams require identifying each change and applying the changes in order. We train a selector on a frozen language model to read each transition. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25235v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Parametric memory allows Large Language Models to internalize knowledge directly into their weights, offering a potentially powerful alternative to retrieval-based memory (RAG). However, existing approaches to parametric memory are difficult to deploy as they largely mirror the Continual Learning (CL) objective of retaining information indefinitely. This is neither sustainable nor sufficient for a memory system, which must govern knowledge across its lifecycle by retaining stable facts, reinforcing recurring observations, updating changed beliefs, and allowing transient information to fade. We propose a system for parametric memory management consisting of a memory substrate (handling information storage and forgetting) and a learned policy (what to remember, how deeply, and for how long). Abstract: Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) now help develop many models published as general solutions. Should generality instead reside in the agent that builds a model for each new task? We examine this question in prognostics and health management (PHM), where every model must work on unseen equipment. Our deployment-style benchmark, NextUnit-Bench, covers 24 public datasets split into 58 folds that hold out units or operating conditions; each agent has two hours to deliver an executable predictor, then run on the hidden units. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24943v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Computational complexity theory offers a principled framework for characterizing the efficiency of computational problems, and Large Language Models (LLMs) can similarly be viewed as computational systems executing a structured process of input, inference-time compute, and output. In this context, the number of generated tokens emerges as a natural and directly observable proxy for inference-time compute. However, we show that the tempting analogy between LLM token length and classical time complexity does not hold. We disprove the hypothesis that inference-time token usage aligns monotonically with classical time complexity, demonstrating a fundamental divergence grounded in how LLMs actually allocate computation during inference. Abstract: The rise of powerful, fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) necessitates robust natural language inference (NLI) systems. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24960v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Converting complex documents into structured knowledge constitutes the critical infrastructure urgently required for deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) in downstream research. However, blind to the Table of Contents (ToC) as a macro-structure, existing bottom-up paradigms rely on localized visual cues, inducing heuristic fragility in high-entropy layouts where visual prominence decouples from logical depth; meanwhile, direct LLM extraction lacks spatial grounding, triggering hallucinations in long contexts. articles.title: Global Importance Estimation for KV Cache Eviction
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24969v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Memory consumption of the key-value (KV) cache remains a central bottleneck for long-context LLM inference. We introduce PRKV, a training-free KV eviction method that estimates multi-hop global token importance by applying Personalized PageRank over attention-induced transition graphs. This enables importance propagation beyond recency or instantaneous attention, without modifying the model. We benchmark PRKV on long-context understanding, sparse retrieval, and chain-of-thought reasoning tasks using multiple LLM families. Under moderate to aggressive compression ratios, including up to 90%, PRKV achieves competitive task performance against established eviction baselines while reducing peak memory usage with low end-to-end overhead. These results demonstrate that multi-hop global influence estimation yields a favorable accuracy--memory trade-off for scalable long-context inference.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24971v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) improves large language model performance at inference time without updating model parameters. However, these gains are not free: in practical deployments, longer prompts directly increase inference cost and latency. Under a fixed token budget, prompt construction therefore becomes a resource-allocation problem. While prior work has often focused on how many examples to include in ICL, we study the complementary question of whether the available budget is better spent on a few long demonstrations or on a larger number of shorter ones. We study this aspect in question answering (QA), by organizing candidate demonstrations into length-based bins and constructing prompts from examples within the same length range under fixed budgets. Abstract: We present CANDID (Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution), an execution-control framework designed to enhance the reliability of local computer-use agents (CUAs) in resource-constrained settings. Abstract: Populations vary along cultural dimensions such as individualism, collectivism, and honor. Abstract: Efforts to keep clinical language models safe have concentrated on what enters and leaves the model, but a manipulated model can return an answer that looks entirely ordinary. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) write fluent financial analyses but miscompute ratios, recall stale prices, and route questions to the wrong tool with high confidence. We ask which component should do each job in a financial question-answering assistant, and study it with FinVeriQA, an open-source multi-agent research prototype over SEC filings and live market data: a compact typed-decision model (Laya) routes each question and screens out advice requests, Python computes every number, retrieval and tools fetch evidence, Mistral-7B writes a cited answer, a code validator checks that cited IDs exist and that numbers match computed notes, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes the pipeline. articles.title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25123v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents often exceed their context windows, forcing them to discard information that may be needed later. Existing context management strategies rely on summarization, masking, or structured memory, requiring decisions about what to preserve or how to retrieve it before future needs are known. However, these methods can introduce lossy compression, potentially discarding details needed for future tasks. To address this limitation, we introduce GrepMem, a simple, lossless, and index-free memory mechanism built on two components: an append-only plain-text log of the agent's complete history and a regular-expression search tool for on-demand recall. Unlike structured memory systems, GrepMem requires no embeddings, retrieval index, memory extraction, or additional models. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25191v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM judges serve as rewards where no answer key exists, in the hope that their knowledge passes to the trained model. In 814 RL runs that teach 7-8B models to answer closed-book questions or abstain, we ask what passes. What a grader knows about single answers stays home. A wrong answer that a judge rewards is memorised for that one question. A model trained with the answer key, or with a far stronger judge, chooses which new questions to answer no better than the untrained model does by sampling 32 answers and abstaining where they disagree; the grader's knowledge adds about one corrected answer per hundred questions. What a grader believes about a kind of question travels. A judge that rejects eleven of the twelve correct training answers about capitals of former states teaches the model to refuse 98% of such capitals on new questions, a loss that accuracy and abstention rates do not reveal. arXiv:2611.25258v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Post-hoc rewriting is used to reduce demographic disparities in LLM-generated text when the source model is inaccessible. A rewriter proposes edits, a selection model chooses among constraint-satisfying candidates, and an independent evaluator uninvolved in either rates pairwise framing disparity. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25289v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Zero-shot large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as text classifiers, but their labels are only useful when we know to what extent we can trust them. We compare black-box methods (verbalised confidence and sampling) with white-box methods that read token probabilities (P(True), and multiple logit-scoring methods using constrained generation). We evaluate eleven open-weight LLMs (1B-32B parameters) on five classification datasets with 3 to 151 labels, measuring classification performance (accuracy, F1-macro), discrimination (AUROC), and calibration (ECE and Brier score). The choice of confidence method rarely impacts accuracy significantly, but logit-based scoring methods lead to much better discrimination (AUROC 0.74-0.77) than black-box methods (AUROC 0.57-0.66). articles.content:

Abstract: Browsers now ship local language models to ordinary endpoints. Google includes Gemini Nano in Chrome to enable productivity features such as summarization, with inference running entirely on the device. These browser-embedded models provide new living-off-the-land opportunities for attackers, each instance a potential post-exploitation engine already installed, signed by the vendor, and invisible to network monitoring. The Gemini model is multimodal, capable of processing files, analyzing screenshots, or conversing with an attacker. articles.title: CoMPASS: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Measuring LLM Reinforcement of Parasocial Behavior
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25109v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Users of conversational LLMs sometimes anthropomorphize these systems, form emotional attachments to them, and become dependent on them. This behavior, known as parasocial attachment, has been linked to multiple documented fatalities. However, public benchmarks for measuring whether LLMs reinforce users' parasocial attachment are lacking: existing work is single-turn, post hoc observational, or focused on extreme user states such as psychosis. We introduce CoMPASS, a multi-turn benchmark for measuring whether LLMs reinforce or resist users' gradually escalating parasocial attachment. CoMPASS is grounded in attachment theory and includes four user personas, three independent escalation dimensions (anthropomorphism, attachment, dependency) applied singly and in combination against a matched control, and a seven-signal scoring rubric. articles.content:

Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can only teach a language model what its reward can recognize. Answer checkers are exact but need a reference answer; learned reward models and LLM judges work everywhere, but their scores are not probabilities. We study RLCDR (Reinforcement Learning from Calibrated Decision Rewards). An LLM converted into a decision model answers a typed question about a response ("is the final answer correct?", "which step is the first error?") with a probability distribution, read in one forward pass, debiased over option orders and calibrated with about a hundred labels. Abstract: Understanding an egocentric environment requires reasoning about how surrounding entities affect the observer's actions. articles.title: Infer3D: Inverse Generative Modeling Enables Robust 3D Reconstruction
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25061v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humans can understand the 3D structure of scenes even from highly unfamiliar or extreme viewpoints. Cognitive science suggests this generalization stems from a top-down generative inference strategy. In contrast, state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction neural networks typically rely on amortized, feedforward inference. While fast, this pattern-matching approach degrades when faced with out-of-distribution (OOD) scene conditions unseen during training. Inspired by the generative nature of human vision, we propose Infer3D, an inverse generative modeling framework that recovers the latent variables of a generative model to best match the monocular input. To prevent degenerate flat outputs, we couple the generative image prior with a frozen 3D lifting network that constrains the optimization space to a valid, multi-view-consistent 3D manifold. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25069v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) offers a promising approach to improving visual reasoning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, not all samples benefit equally from privileged visual guidance, and uniform token supervision can dilute visually grounded signals. We propose VisAlloc, a dual-level framework combining sample-level visual filtering with token-level counterfactual reweighting. A fixed paired-teacher filter retains samples answered correctly from an evidence-centered positive crop but incorrectly from a spatially displaced negative crop. At the token level, both EMA teachers score the same student-generated response, and their absolute log-probability differences measure view sensitivity. articles.content:

Abstract: Localizing object boundaries is important for embodied visual systems, since small boundary errors can change the inferred geometry of physical surfaces. We study whether deep stereo models produce boundaries consistent with simple shape priors when local image and disparity cues are weak. We create a synthetic stereo dataset consisting of objects drawn from a highly constrained family of shapes, with randomized depth, slant, color and texture. Despite the simplicity of this shape space, we find that several state-of-the-art stereo models retain systematic boundary errors, even when finetuned or trained from scratch on the dataset. We then introduce a simple generative stereo model that jointly predicts disparity and a distance field representing object boundaries. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25126v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cross-modal knowledge distillation can incur negative transfer when source-modality supervision conflicts with the target modality's discriminative characteristics. We propose TALD, a two-stage framework for Transferability-Aware Logit Disentanglement in class-aligned logit space. Guided by task-dependent self-benefiting and cross-modal exclusivity criteria, a Residual Disentangler decomposes logits from a teacher and an independently trained target-modality reference student into modality-general and modality-specific components. A Sample-Adaptive Modulator regulates decomposition constraints and sample-specific fusion weights. The learned modality-general components are then adaptively fused to supervise the final student. Across five benchmarks spanning vision, audio, and text, TALD achieves the largest mean accuracy gain and highest positive-transfer frequency among the compared methods. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25168v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A calibrated decision model can predict how often each answer is chosen. The same prediction can reflect disagreement among people who are confident in their choices or uncertainty among people who share a belief. Disagreement calls for identifying whose perspective applies, while uncertainty calls for gathering more evidence. Standard post-training scores a single prediction against one observed choice at a time, learning the pooled distribution without distinguishing these two sources of uncertainty. We introduce Belief-Grouped Policy Optimization (BGPO). The policy proposes a list of beliefs, estimates their prevalence, and predicts a choice distribution for each. During training, BGPO uses Bayes' rule to estimate how likely each belief was to generate an observed choice. These estimates weight the choice's contribution to each belief's log-score reward. Abstract: JEPA-based video encoders learn strong representations for video and image understanding through prediction in latent space. Consequently, the learned representations may not reliably support matching across different camera viewpoints. To solve this problem, we introduce multi-view predictive post-training to strengthen cross-view instance and temporal correspondence while retaining independent single-view inference. A shared encoder processes masked context views independently, and a training-time predictor jointly predicts latent tokens for masked context regions and a fully held-out view. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25179v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. Passing an expert demonstration shows that a checker accepts one way of completing the task. Learned policies, however, may stop after partial progress or complete the task in a different way. A checker may then accept an incomplete execution (phantom success) or reject an execution that satisfies the instruction (silent failure). In this paper, we introduce SimAudit, an LLM-based pipeline that audits success checkers against task instructions. SimAudit analyzes the instruction and checker code to identify scenarios where the two may disagree, recreates those scenarios in simulation, and runs the original checker. articles.title: Identity World Model: Recognizing People in an Imagined Latent World
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25204v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Whole-body human recognition has advanced rapidly with large vision models. However, existing methods remain fragile under real-world variations, as they tie identity to transient cues such as clothing, texture, pose, or viewpoint. We argue that a robust recognizer should not merely learn to ignore these cues, but imagine how a person would be represented if they changed. To this end, we propose IDWorld, an identity world model: just as a latent world model predicts the features of a scene after an action, IDWorld predicts how a person would be represented under a changed condition. In a single forward pass, IDWorld imagines these counterfactual features under shared canonical conditions, such as the same outfit, a fixed view, or a bare silhouette, without rendering any pixels. articles.title: Recurrent Vision Language Models Solve the Shell Game
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25210v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tracking a hidden object through a video is effortless for humans, yet it remains a bottleneck for vision language models (VLMs). In the shell game, where a ball is hidden under one of several identical cups that are then swapped, VLMs that answer directly stay near chance, thinking models fail on long games, and fine-tuning learns only the lengths it has seen. We argue that the limit is serial computation: each swap must be composed with the last result, and a VLM of fixed depth has only a fixed number of state transitions for it. To address this, we propose RecurrentVLM, which makes every attention layer of a pretrained VLM recur over time by computing the keys and values of finished frame groups from the layer's own output. Abstract: Can a frontier model repair a vision-language model (VLM) by rewriting its weights? Small reasoning VLMs such as Qwen3.5 need such a repair: in thinking mode they fall into loops on many image questions, repeating themselves until the token limit, spending the whole budget and losing the answer. Abstract: We extend PoseTReID with online appearance-bank matching (Gallery) and a residual-conflict guard for registered SVM recognition. All methods use supplied ground-truth (GT) person boxes. We average all-box assessment IDF1/HOTA equally across videos. On six SportsMOT clips, StrongSORT leads standalone trackers (79.44/84.72%) and exceeds both Gallery variants. articles.title: CalibCache: Cache-to-Full Feature Dynamics Calibration for Diffusion Transformers
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25296v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion Transformers generate high-quality images, but iterative sampling remains computationally expensive. Feature caching reduces the number of full network evaluations, yet its approximation error can become more severe under short sampling schedules, where fewer full-compute steps and a coarser sampling grid can make history-based extrapolation less reliable. In this paper, we propose CalibCache, a lightweight offline calibration method that corrects systematic discrepancies between cached and full-compute feature dynamics. Specifically, CalibCache calibrates feature acceleration, defined as the second-order finite difference across sampling steps. Using only a single pair of full-compute and naive-cache trajectories at each setting, CalibCache fits scalar acceleration maps offline by centered least squares. These maps are then applied during sampling without additional full-network evaluations or online optimization. Across FLUX.

Abstract: GUI grounding maps a screenshot and a natural language instruction to the coordinates of the intended interface element. Existing approaches improve grounding through visual scaling, instruction scaling, and sampling scaling, yet it remains unclear which grounding bottlenecks these strategies address and where their gains saturate. To address this gap, we introduce ScaleDiag, a controlled diagnostic framework that isolates the effects of visual input, instruction information, and prediction sampling on GUI grounding by independently varying target scale and surrounding context, target-specific information and auxiliary descriptions, and candidate coverage and selection, respectively. We evaluate ScaleDiag across five benchmarks and up to eight vision-language models and find that each scaling strategy operates within a much narrower regime than commonly assumed. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25005v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent work on human-scene interaction (HSI) generation moves from single interactions to long-horizon interaction, where a language-model agent plans and executes a sequence of interactions in a 3D scene under one instruction. However, existing agents struggle in challenging everyday scenarios (e.g., picking up a toy and throwing it into a basket) because they lack spatial control over the motion and quantitative feedback on its execution, and they often fail to complete the interaction sequence. To address these gaps, we present Inhabitant, a training-free agent framework in which the agent specifies each motion through positions, paths and poses, measures how the executed interaction deviates from its intent, and revises the control specification accordingly. articles.title: Mapping the Wind to Find the Source: Online Physics-Informed Gas Source Localization with Mobile Robots
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25067v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gas Source Localization (GSL) with mobile robots is challenging because wind and gas measurements are spatially sparse, noisy, and potentially affected by robot motion. Indoor airflow can vary substantially across space, while detailed environmental layouts, boundary conditions, or precomputed airflow fields are often unavailable. Moreover, hazardous sources must be localized as quickly as possible, making exhaustive exploration impractical. This paper presents a lightweight physics-informed probabilistic framework for efficient GSL under spatially varying indoor airflow. As the robot navigates, it continuously collects wind and gas measurements and reconstructs the spatially varying airflow field online. The estimated wind field drives a forward dispersion model that predicts the gas pattern for each candidate source location. articles.title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25105v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample. Built from a pretrained single-robot world-action backbone, MAWAM jointly denoises all robots' action and future-view tokens through cross-agent attention, while preserving a separate control interface for each robot. MAWAM achieves the highest success on all three real-robot tasks (laundry-bag collection, bath-towel folding, and umbrella handover), with 67.8% mean success, 18.9 percentage points above MA-VLA trained on the same demonstrations and cameras. arXiv:2611.25134v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Visual world models enable effective short-horizon goal-conditioned planning, such as reaching nearby targets and pushing objects over short distances, by predicting candidate action outcomes and comparing their representations with a goal representation. However, extending this approach to long-horizon tasks is challenging: prediction errors accumulate over extended rollouts, while latent-space similarity to distant goals provides limited guidance for ranking candidate outcomes. Existing methods address these limitations by introducing intermediate subgoals, either generated by learned models or selected from experience memory. Generated subgoals can contain hallucinations or be inaccurate in aspects such as object positions and timing. articles.title: Old-School Planners Drive (Sometimes) Better Than Learned Ones
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25138v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: End-to-end driving models learn to plan from data, and hand-written planners are widely treated as a thing of the past. We test whether this is justified: we implement sixteen textbook planners, each combining a path source (reference line, A*, hybrid A*, RRT*) with a trajectory method (Frenet lattice, nonlinear optimization, $s$--$t$ search, dynamic window), and evaluate them on three benchmarks: open loop on nuScenes, closed loop on nuPlan with ground-truth perception, and photorealistic closed loop on HUGSIM. On HUGSIM, they replace only the planner of the end-to-end model UniAD and read its frozen perception, without an HD map or other privileged information. On nuScenes and nuPlan, the best textbook planners are competitive (L2 error of 0.735\,m against 0.947\,m for UniAD's planner; a nuPlan score of 79.3 against 76.1 for the rule-based PDM-Closed on Test14-hard with reactive agents). articles.title: From Self-Play RL to Constrained Control: Distilling DiffMPC Students with DAgger
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25197v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Self-play reinforcement learning (RL) produces strong driving policies, but these policies are hard to verify or interpret. Differentiable model predictive control (DiffMPC) can enforce explicit constraints, but it is usually trained by imitating logged data or with costly RL. To add constraints to an already trained policy, we keep a PPO teacher's backbone and replace its action head with a DiffMPC that enforces road boundary half-planes and agent ellipses. We then distill the student with DAgger in the teacher's self-play simulator. Over 9 seeds, the constrained student of a smaller teacher matches its teacher on nuPlan and beats it on CARLA and on out-of-distribution Waymo scenes. For a stronger teacher, the student has fewer failures on nuPlan and Waymo, while staying level on CARLA. Its distillation takes no more than 30% of the teacher's training time.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25199v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adapting robot policies to out-of-distribution (OOD) settings with limited real-world data remains a key bottleneck to generalist robots. The multimodality and scarcity of robotics data lead end-to-end approaches to overfit and break under small distribution shifts. Test-time adaptation can alleviate this by correcting frozen policies at inference, but most methods ground their correction in a signal learned implicitly from robotic datasets, making it susceptible to the same shifts as the policy it corrects. Recent methods that instead exploit explicit spatial information are typically limited to coarse corrections, missing the nuanced, task-relevant motion most manipulation tasks require. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25215v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous navigation in diverse real-world environments remains one of the greatest challenges in robotics. It demands both robust low-level motion control to handle diverse terrain and high-level reasoning to interpret environmental cues. We present ROAM (Robust Open-world Autonomous Mobility), a system that enables legged robots to perform kilometer-scale navigation in complex alpine and urban settings. ROAM combines the world knowledge of a Vision-Language Model (VLM), pre-trained on internet-scale data, with robust locomotion and local planning policies learned in simulation via reinforcement learning (RL). The VLM provides common-sense reasoning and semantic interpretation of the scene, assessing risks, interpreting signs, and producing semantic labels with associated navigation costs. articles.content:

Abstract: Ferrofluids are liquids containing magnetic nanoparticles, enabling shape control through external magnetic fields. This deformability supports their use as soft robotic bodies that can navigate confined spaces and manipulate objects. Their nonlinear continuum dynamics, however, make reliable control challenging. Existing work shows how spatial magnetic fields from electromagnet arrays can establish and maintain desired ferrofluid configurations. A complementary objective is to exploit the fluid's dynamics under limited actuation to reach prescribed shapes that may not be sustainable at equilibrium. Here, we use deep model-based reinforcement learning to control these transient shapes. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25243v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can propose multi-step manipulation plans, but they have no grounded model of how a scene will change, and the pixel-level world models that could check those plans are slow and drift over long horizons. We present Verify2Act, a modular verification framework that separates semantic action proposal from latent physical verification. A VLM proposes candidate plans, a latent world model (V2A-WM) imagines each of them in the DINOv2 feature space, and a dual-head critic checks the imagined rollouts for temporal consistency and goal satisfaction before anything is executed. V2A-WM extends recent flow-matching world models with cross-attention action grounding and a causal temporal history window. We deploy the full system on a low-cost robot arm, training the world model and critic only on data generated in a digital twin. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25249v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic cyber-physical systems rely on perception and state estimation to support autonomous decisions. Degraded, inconsistent, or manipulated sensor observations can therefore propagate through an autonomous pipeline and create security-relevant failures. This work presents a synthetic Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (C-UAS) testbed developed in NVIDIA Isaac Sim for repeatable stress testing of perception and tracking algorithms supporting agentic decision-making. A simplified quadrotor follows scripted trajectories while co-located virtual sensors generate synchronized RGB, RTX LiDAR, and illustrative IR-like observations. The testbed varies target range, motion, clutter, occlusion, and sensor availability, with future stress cases including sensor dropout, temporal misalignment, cross-modal disagreement, and false observations. Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve vision-language-action (VLA) policies beyond imitation, but humanoid exploration is unsafe and simulator RL can exploit residual sim-to-real gaps. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25254v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous robots may need to adapt both their task plans and architectural configurations as operating conditions change. These decisions are interdependent: architectural configurations determine which actions a robot can perform, while task plans determine which capabilities are required. This paper presents PLANTA, an ontology-mediated approach to task and architecture co-adaptation that considers these dependencies during mission planning. PLANTA uses an ontology expressed in the Web Ontology Language to represent architectural alternatives and their associated functional and quality requirements, while the Planning Domain Definition Language defines task actions and mission goals. By automatically translating and integrating these models, PLANTA enables joint planning of task and reconfiguration actions. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25202v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Crisis and disaster governance increasingly relies on technologies that sense, classify and act faster than humans can. Drone swarms coordinated with human operators, known as human-swarm teaming, provide a productive case to review the field of crisis governance. They promise better situational awareness in disaster response, but they also raise questions about human control, responsibility, surveillance, triage, dual use and public legitimacy. This report maps the ethical and societal territory that HST opens up. It unpacks this territory with a 3i-framework, the Interface, where operators and swarms work together, the Infrastructure, where organisations distribute tasks, decisions and blame, and the Imaginary, where law, policy and shared societal assumptions define what a crisis is and which interventions it justifies. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25320v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Residual reinforcement learning corrects an imitation-trained base policy using a limited budget of environment interaction. In a task with several phases, this budget must be divided among the phases, and the phase in which the base policy fails is not necessarily the phase in which a correction most improves task completion. We formalize this distinction through the completion gain: the change in full-task completion probability when, during a single phase, a state-feedback controller replaces selected components of the base policy's action. We decompose the completion gain into the probability of reaching the phase and the conditional improvement in completion from the start of the phase, and we estimate it from paired episodes. articles.content:
arXiv:2509.21961v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Learning-based planners are sensitive to the long-tailed distribution of driving data. Common maneuvers dominate datasets, while dangerous or rare scenarios are sparse. This imbalance can bias models toward the frequent cases and degrade performance on critical scenarios. To tackle this problem, we compare balancing strategies for sampling training data and find reweighting by trajectory pattern an effective approach. We then present FlowDrive, a flow-matching trajectory planner that learns a conditional rectified flow to map noise directly to trajectory distributions with few flow-matching steps. We further introduce moderated, in-the-loop guidance that injects small perturbation between flow steps to systematically increase trajectory diversity while remaining scene-consistent. articles.content:
arXiv:2602.07629v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We propose LCLA (Language-Conditioned Latent Alignment), a framework for vision-language navigation that learns modular perception-action interfaces by aligning sensory observations to a latent representation of an expert policy. The expert is first trained with privileged state information, inducing a latent space sufficient for control, after which its latent interface and action head are frozen. A lightweight adapter is then trained to map raw visual-language observations, via a frozen vision-language model, into the expert's latent space, reducing the problem of visuomotor learning to supervised latent alignment rather than end-to-end policy optimization. This decoupling enforces a stable contract between perception and control, enabling expert behavior to be reused across sensing modalities and environmental variations. articles.content:
arXiv:2602.18224v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models often bundle architectural changes with different pretraining data, backbone scales, and optimization recipes, obscuring what actually drives progress. We introduce SimVLA, a deliberately minimal VLA, a standard vision-language backbone with a lightweight continuous-action head, as a controlled testbed for this attribution problem; our contribution is methodological and empirical (a controlled attribution study and a minimal-baseline calibration), not a new technique. articles.title: 苹果 20 周年款 iPhone 渲染图曝光：整机如一块玻璃，四曲面带来“无边框”观感
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，YouTube 频道 AppleTrack 昨日（11 月 19 日）更新视频，分享了苹果 20 周年款 iPhone（该信源称其为 iPhone XX）的渲染图。消息源称本次渲染基于可信泄露信息制作，显示 iPhone XX 采用全玻璃工业设计、曲面显示屏、触觉按键、苹果设计的摄像头传感器以及全新的电池技术。IT之家查询公开信息，AppleTrack 由 Sam Kohl 运营，内容以汇总传闻、追踪爆料源和部分独家消息为主，会交叉验证马克 · 古尔曼、郭明錤、The Information 等信息来源，此外 MacWorld 等主流媒体也会采信 AppleTrack 跟进报道，因此其渲染图片有一定可信度，但苹果官方发布前，相关信息仅供参考。延伸阅读初代 iPhone 于 2007 年 1 月首次亮相、同年 6 月 29 日上市，因此 2027 年恰逢 iPhone 问世 20 周年。据供应链消息，苹果计划跳过 iPhone 19 的命名，2027 年的新机将直接以 iPhone 20（也有 iPhone XX 的叫法）命名，该机型预计定位对标十周年的 iPhone X，于 2027 年 9 月发布，不会出现在 2026 年秋季发布会上。这与苹果 2017 年的做法如出一辙 —— 当年正值 iPhone 问世十周年，苹果跳过 iPhone 9，直接推出以罗马数字“X”（代表 10）命名的 iPhone X，后者于 2017 年 9 月 12 日发布、11 月 3 日开售。据爆料，20 周年版 iPhone 的内部工程机代号为“Glasswing”，暗示全玻璃机身方向。据科技媒体 MacRumors 于 2026 年 11 月汇总、验证的供应链消息，20 周年版 iPhone（上市后可能命名为 iPhone 20 Pro）有望迎来四曲面全玻璃外观、屏下 Face ID、屏下前置摄像头、固态按键、新一代 OLED 屏幕、A21 Pro 芯片、自研图像传感器等全方位升级。文中提到的“苹果设计的摄像头传感器”或指向苹果自研 CMOS 图像传感器，其采用 LOFIC（横向溢出积分电容）次世代 HDR 成像技术，通过在单像素中整合线性与对数两种电荷容纳方式提升动态范围，让手机在大光比场景下呈现更丰富细节，最高或实现 20 档动态范围，接近高端电影摄影机水平。文中提到的“全新的电池技术”或为硅阳极电池。相比传统石墨阳极，硅阳极单位重量可储存更多锂离子，有望在不增大机身的前提下延长续航。此外，该机还有望搭载与无边界视觉相呼应的“液态玻璃”（Liquid Glass）系统 UI，界面控件、动画与机身玻璃质感相互配合，呈现整机如同一整块玻璃的观感。另据博主 @数码闲聊站 爆料，iPhone 20 Pro 屏幕尺寸约为 6.41 英寸、分辨率 2686*1236，iPhone 20 Pro Max 约为 6.96 英寸、分辨率 2912*1340，苹果正在测试无边四曲面设计和小灵动岛打孔方案。

articles.title: 能让 iPhone 跑安卓 App 的虚拟机 Andarium 被苹果 App Store 火速下架
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，一款名为“Andarium”软件日前上架苹果 App Store 平台，这是一款安卓虚拟机软件，支持在 iPhone 和 iPad 上运行 Android 应用，引发网络热议。Andarium 的开发者 xieyi 今日发文，表示 Andarium 已被苹果从 App Store 下架。xieyi 晒出的截图内容称：经过重新评估，我们发现该应用不符合应用审核指南。具体来说，我们发现该应用违反了以下规定：指南 2.5.2 和 1.1 一一性能一一软件要求我们注意到，该应用包含并非专注于受支持苹果平台体验的功能。具体来说，你的应用允许用户在 iOS 平台上复制安卓操作系统。下一步由于提交中包含不良内容的严重性，该 App 不再有资格获得 App Store 的批准。xieyi 表示，后续该应用只能通过 GitHub 更新，以侧载方式安装了。xieyi 还称，Andarium 首个发布到 App Store 的版本就已经具备非常良好的应用兼容性。关于应用崩溃的报告非常少。可惜他没能完成 AOT 编译并推送更新，而更新能根据工作负载提升 60% 到 100% 的性能。IT之家附 Andarium 开源地址：https://github.com/imxieyi/Kernarium

articles.title: Sensor Tower 估算《GTA 6》首日销量约 2458 万份，收入达 23.6 亿美元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，路透社援引 Sensor Tower 数据称，截至当地时间 11 月 19 日晚间，Rockstar Games 新作《侠盗猎车手 6》（GTA 6）游戏累计销量达到 2458 万份，预计可为 Take-Two 带来约 23.6 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 157.93 亿元人民币）收入。按照这一估算，《GTA 6》的首日销售收入接近《GTA 5》2013 年首日约 8 亿美元收入的 3 倍。后者长期被视为首发日 24 小时内销量表现最好的游戏之一。Take-Two 是 Rockstar Games 的母公司，旗下还拥有《荒野大镖客》和《NBA 2K》等游戏系列。尽管《GTA 6》预购于今年 6 月开启，但公司一直没有公布具体销量，仅表示市场需求前所未有，远超预期。Take-Two 此前表示，截至 2025 年 12 月，第九世代主机保有量约为 1.38 亿台；公司本月发布的后续材料则将截至 2026 年 6 月的数据列为 1.3 亿台。Take-Two 首席执行官 Strauss Zelnick 本月早些时候在财报电话会议上表示，《GTA 6》受到广泛期待，消费者表现出极高的热情，且媒体评价也非常积极，但公司绝不会提前开香槟。Take-Two 预计，游戏发售后的 2027 财年第三季度净预订额将达到创纪录的 81 亿美元（现汇率约合 542.05 亿元人民币）。公司还说明，终极版中价值 20 美元的部分将计入经常性消费者支出。在营销方面，Take-Two 为《GTA 6》投入的开发成本估计达到 10 亿美元（现汇率约合 66.92 亿元人民币）或更多，使其成为娱乐行业成本最高的项目之一。Sensor Tower 估算，Netflix 于今年 8 月推出的《GTA 6》宣传视频 Extended Look，帮助游戏预购量增长至此前的 6 倍。此外，游戏发售期间，故事背景参考现实迈阿密的 NBA 球队举办了以 Vice City 为主题的比赛。公司还计划在周末举办名为《GTA VI: The Festival》的音乐活动，邀请格莱美奖得主 Cardi B、嘻哈音乐制作人 Metro Boomin 以及说唱歌手 Travis Scott 等艺人参加。随着游戏正式发售，投资者目前更加关注 Take-Two 对 PC 版本及在线多人模式的后续安排。在线多人模式能够通过持续更新和玩家消费，为游戏带来长期收入。部分行业分析师预计，《GTA 6》PC 版本及在线模式可能在 2027 年推出。不过，Take-Two 尚未正式公布这两项内容的具体上线时间。

articles.title: 吉利董事长李书福：一般性的传统大学已不适应 AI 时代人才培养需求，必将诞生一批新型大学
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，据新浪财经睿见 Economy 报道，吉利控股集团董事长李书福今日在 2026 芯位教育论坛上表示，AI 时代的大学生活与传统大学有着划时代的区别，知识传播与教授方法已经发生根本性改变。李书福说：“传统大学就像传统的百货公司、传统的超市，而人工智能时代诞生的大学，就像阿里巴巴、腾讯、京东、字节跳动。”他回忆，当年的上海第一百货、第四百货和杭州解放路百货大楼曾经“不得了”，如今都很困难了，都变成了电商。“这两种模式是完全不一样的起点、完全不一样的效果。”在新模式下，学生可以根据自己的喜好和实际情况安排学习节奏。他坦言，一般性的传统大学，其人才培养体系与能力结构已经不适应人工智能时代人才培养的迫切需求。“人工智能时代必将诞生一批与这个时代相匹配的新型大学。”李书福表示，长期以来，吉利坚持“既是一个企业，也是一座学校”的经营发展理念，吉利汽车工业创业初期，依托的是吉利技师学院、吉利技工学校，在造车之前先把学校办起来，有了人才、有了技师技工，吉利才开始生产汽车。他进一步指出，人工智能时代更需要人才培养和知识更新，但培养的方法、学习的内容一定要与时代进步相匹配。数据库里的知识并不等于每个人都已掌握，大语言模型再聪明，也不等于每个人自然就变聪明了。IT之家查询公开资料获悉，吉利目前已形成从中高职教育到本科、研究生教育的多层次办学体系，旗下包括吉利学院、三亚学院、湘潭理工学院、浙江汽车职业技术学院、湖南吉利汽车职业技术学院、三亚理工职业学院等。李书福还表示，当前世界正面临新型全球化与地缘政治的双重挑战，变化剧烈、冲突频发。在这样的背景下，吉利控股集团将继续协同旗下教育与人才板块的几所学校联合培养人才，并把这一培养规模扩大到全球，招收本硕博学生，培养新型全球化人才。

articles.title: 全球限 250 辆：保时捷联合推出电动复刻车型 550 J，最高时速 80 km/h
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，汽车媒体 electrek 昨日（11 月 19 日）发布博文，报道称保时捷与英国微型汽车制造商 Hedley Studios 合作，推出经典赛车 550 Spyder 的电动复刻车型 550 J，全球限量 250 辆。IT之家注：550 J 由 Hedley Studios 手工制造、获得保时捷官方授权，并非保时捷自行生产的常规量产电动车。新车按原车尺寸的 80% 打造，仍可容纳两名成年人，计划于 11 月 21 日至 22 日在迪拜“Icons of Porsche”活动上公开亮相。550 J 采用钢管空间车架和手工成型碳纤维车身，车重约 350 公斤。标准版搭载 48 伏电气系统及 8 千瓦电机，最高时速约 65 公里，续航最高约 50 公里。选装 RS 套件后，电机功率增至 16 千瓦，并增加电池，最高时速提升至约 80 公里 / 小时，续航提升至 80 公里，同时配备打孔制动盘和可调悬架。复古细节是新车的一大看点，木质轮圈方向盘搭配三圆仪表，原来的燃油表改为电量表，阻风门拉杆变成驾驶模式选择器，充电接口则藏在镀铬加油口盖下。项目历时 6 年开发，开发团队参考了保时捷原始工程图纸、档案及博物馆藏车。新车限量 250 辆，支持历史赛车涂装和个性化配色，起售价 6.95 万英镑（现汇率约合 61 万元人民币），不含税费及选装费用。以上图源：保时捷

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，当地时间 11 月 19 日，群晖发布安全公告，确认 DSM 系统存在一个严重安全漏洞 CVE-2026-120382，CVSS 3.1 评分高达 9.8 分。该漏洞位于群晖 DSM 的 OAuth API，攻击者无需身份验证即可远程读取或写入 NAS 中的任意文件，甚至能够发起拒绝服务攻击。根据群晖安全公告，该漏洞属于命令参数分隔符未正确处理问题（CWE-88），影响 DSM 多个版本。其 CVSS 评分为 9.8 分，攻击者无需登录，也不需要用户进行任何交互，即可尝试利用该漏洞。群晖目前尚未公开漏洞的具体利用细节，但已经确认问题涉及官方 OAuth Service 套件。该套件用于提供 OAuth API 及相关身份验证服务。考虑到部分 DSM 分支尚未提供修复更新，群晖建议暂时无法升级的用户停用 OAuth Service 套件，以降低安全风险。用户可以进入 DSM 的套件中心，找到 OAuth Service 并选择停用。需要注意的是，停用该套件可能影响依赖 OAuth 身份验证的登录及相关服务，企业用户应提前检查现有授权配置，避免影响正常业务运行。根据群晖官方安全公告，目前涉及的产品及修复版本如下：DSM 7.4：升级至 DSM 7.4.1-90080-2 或更高版本，计划于 2026 年 11 月 20 日发布。DSM 7.3：升级至 DSM 7.3.2-86009-6 或更高版本，计划于 2026 年 11 月 20 日发布。DSM 7.2.2：修复工作仍在进行，群晖建议升级至 DSM 7.3.2-86009-6 或更高版本。DSM 7.2.1：修复工作仍在进行，群晖建议升级至 DSM 7.3.2-86009-6 或更高版本。DSM 7.1：修复工作仍在进行。DSM 6.2：需升级至 DSM 6.2.4-25556-9 或更高版本。IT之家注意到，群晖公告还将 BeeStation OS 1.5 列为受影响产品，目前相关修复工作仍在进行。APM 1.2、APM 2.0、DSM Enterprise 1.0 以及 SRM 1.2、1.3 则不受此次漏洞影响。相关阅读：《群晖：黑客利用 2024 年 12 月已修复漏洞攻击，用户应尽快更新 DSM 操作系统》

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，广汽传祺越 7 两驱激光雷达版 SUV 今日上市，官方指导价 19.58 万元，限时权益价 18.78 万元。IT之家注意到，新车延续“方盒子”车身轮廓，前脸为封闭式设计，搭配纵向排列的三颗日间行车灯，车顶安装激光雷达，前翼子板处配备传感器硬件。车尾采用蓄光组合式尾灯，直射与反射灯组结合；车门采用双色悬浮式门把手。车身尺寸方面，该车长宽高分别为 5045x2004x1933mm，轴距 2900mm，接近角 30°、离去角 33°，空载离地间隙 230mm，空气悬架升至最高时可达 310mm。座舱方面，越 7 是广汽星灵架构 4.0 的首发车型，搭载星际视界智能座舱系统，由 1.1 米 MiniLED 全景贯穿星际屏、星环视界与 15.6 英寸中控屏组成。官方称，贯穿屏支持 55 种功能组件自由拖拽，内置性能、智驾、萌宠、通勤、越野五大主题模式。乘坐空间上，第二排腿部最大空间 1015mm、头部空间 1020mm，配备 170mm 二排电动滑轨与 127° 可调座椅。前排为十层结构真皮座椅，支持加热、通风、按摩，放倒后可形成 1.9 米纯平大床；车内配备 5.7L 宽温域冷暖箱，温域 -6℃~50℃。动力方面，该车系统综合最大功率 550kW，轮端总扭矩 10000N・m，百公里加速 4.2 秒，WLTC 工况百公里馈电油耗 6.21L。新车搭载 46 度宁德时代骁遥电池，CLTC 纯电续航 261km，综合续航 1352km，30%-80% 快充需 15 分钟。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，科技媒体 SamMobile 昨日（11 月 19 日）发布博文，报道称在 One UI 9.5 首个 Beta 测试版中，三星正在为天气（Weather）应用酝酿 AI 升级，在用户出发前提醒其查看目的地天气。IT之家援引博文介绍，系统识别到用户计划前往另一座城市后，天气应用会显示“出发前查看天气”提示。用户点击“试试”（Try it），即可查看目的地预报。在后台运行方面，该功能涉及三星正在开发的 Personal Agent Core（PAC）系统。该系统可结合多个 One UI 和 Google 应用中的上下文信息，提供个性化体验。例如，当用户在其他地区安排了约会、会议，或手机检测到即将搭乘的跨城航班后，系统便可利用相关信息，触发目的地天气查看提示。

articles.title: 腾讯 Hy4 正式开源，混元 LLM 系列实现全量开放
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，腾讯混元团队今日宣布 Hy4 大模型正式开源，模型权重已在 GitHub、Hugging Face、ModelScope 和 GitCode 四个平台同步上线，开发者可自行下载部署。至此，混元 LLM 系列已完成全部开源，覆盖 Hy3 preview、Hy3、Hy4 preview、Hy4 及 Hy4 flash 等版本。Hy4 正式版最早于 11 月 4 日发布，本次开源的是此前预告的模型权重。Hy4 采用 MoE 混合专家架构，总参数 770B，激活参数 49B，上下文窗口突破 100 万 Token。IT之家此前报道，与旗舰版 Hy4 同步开放的还有主打性价比的 Hy4 flash。Hy4 flash 总参数约 2200 亿，其中包含约 635 亿 Engram 参数，每个 Token 仅激活约 120 亿参数，同样支持最高 100 万 Token 的上下文窗口，并支持文本与图像输入。两者形成从旗舰能力到低成本规模化落地的梯次搭配。开源协议方面，Hy4 及 Hy4 preview 采用 Apache 2.0 许可证，允许商业使用与修改。腾讯混元同步发布了 Hy4 模型安全评估卡片（System Card），披露了网络安全与生物安全等维度的评估结果。据官方说明，Hy4 训练数据仅纳入 PoC 生成、漏洞修复等防守性网络安全内容，剔除了漏洞利用、逆向工程与渗透等攻击性数据；腾讯玄武与科恩实验室的审计未发现明显的进攻性能力风险。参考资料[GitHub] https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy4[Hugging Face] https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4[ModelScope] https://modelscope.cn/models/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy4[GitCode] https://ai.gitcode.com/tencent_hunyuan/Hy4[GGUF] https://huggingface.co/AngelSlim/Hy4-GGUF[开源协议] https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4/blob/main/LICENSE[模型安全评估卡片] https://hy.tencent.ai/Hy4_system_card.pdf

articles.title: 字节回应“原抖音 CEO 张楠、原飞书 CEO 谢欣将离职”：信息不准确
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，据新浪科技今日报道，有媒体报道称，原抖音 CEO 张楠、原飞书 CEO 谢欣将从字节跳动离职。张楠离职后，剪映和即梦 AI 将由两位高管接管。其中，支颖接管剪映，朱骏接管即梦 AI。对此，字节相关负责人回应称，该信息不准确。IT之家从公开资料获悉，谢欣 2014 年加入字节跳动，担任字节副总裁，最早负责效率工程与 HR 系统（飞书 People）；2016 年牵头立项 Lark（飞书前身），2019 年飞书对外商业化，并同步出海 Lark。谢欣早期同时兼任字节 HRVP。张楠早期创业做图片社区产品图吧，2014 年该项目被字节跳动收购，其带团队加入字节跳动，负责 UGC 业务。2016 年，张楠牵头孵化抖音、火山小视频，并带队推出轻颜相机、剪映；2018 年出任抖音 CEO，2020 年升任字节跳动（中国）CEO，统筹国内今日头条、抖音、西瓜、搜索等全部核心业务；2024 年卸任抖音集团 CEO，转而负责剪映和即梦 AI。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，数码博主 @i冰宇宙 今天（11 月 20 日）发布微博，指出：“三星手机终于换帅了！崔元俊正式上位，卢泰文交出 MX 事业部大权”，并对比崔元俊和卢泰文的背景和以往行事风格。IT之家此前报道，三星宣布调整核心业务管理架构，在联席 CEO 全永铉和卢泰文的领导下，黄尚俊（Sang Joon Hwang）晋升为总裁，出任存储业务负责人；崔元俊（Won-Joon Choi）则接任移动业务负责人。三星 MX（Mobile eXperience Business）事业部是三星旗下负责 Galaxy 手机及相关移动设备、软件与生态体验的核心业务部门。对此 @i冰宇宙 在微博中写道：三星手机终于换帅了！崔元俊正式上位，卢泰文交出 MX 事业部大权11 月 20 日，三星电子正式宣布 2027 年度高管人事调整。这次调整中，最值得关注的消息来了：崔元俊（Won-Joon Choi）正式接替卢泰文（TM Roh），成为三星电子 MX 移动体验事业部负责人！这意味着，三星 Galaxy 手机业务正式迎来新的掌舵人！过去几年，卢泰文一直是三星手机业务的核心人物。从 Galaxy S 系列到 Z Fold 折叠屏，再到 One UI 的软件发展，三星手机近年来的产品路线都与他的管理密切相关。如今，他正式卸任 MX 事业部负责人，将更多精力投入整个 DX 事业部的管理，以及机器人等未来业务。而接替他的崔元俊，拥有深厚的技术研发背景，长期参与三星旗舰手机的研发工作，并曾主导 Galaxy S26、Z Fold8 等产品的开发。如今从 MX 事业部首席运营官晋升为负责人，意味着他将直接掌管三星手机业务的未来发展。我认为，这可能是近年来三星手机业务最值得期待的一次高层调整。为什么这么说？过去几年，三星 Galaxy 旗舰手机给人的感觉越来越保守。硬件升级幅度有限，产品创新节奏放缓，One UI 虽然不断进步，但在系统动画、交互细节、流畅度以及软件体验方面，与中国手机厂商相比仍有明显差距。现在，一位拥有深厚技术背景、长期参与旗舰研发的高管正式接管 MX 事业部，至少让我们看到了改变的可能性。当然，崔元俊上位并不意味着三星会立刻改变产品策略。Galaxy S27 的研发已经推进了一段时间，真正能够全面体现新负责人理念的产品，可能还需要更长时间。我尤其期待他能在三个方面有所突破：第一，让 Galaxy 旗舰硬件重新变得激进；第二，让三星折叠屏继续引领行业创新；第三，真正重视 One UI 的软件体验，尤其是动画、交互响应和系统细节。值得注意的是，卢泰文并没有离开三星管理核心。他仍然担任三星电子 CEO 和 DX 事业部负责人，崔元俊未来仍将在他的领导体系下开展工作。但无论如何，三星手机的一个时代已经翻篇了。从卢泰文到崔元俊，Galaxy 迎来了新的掌舵人。我希望这次换帅，能够成为三星手机重新找回创新精神的起点。崔元俊，接下来就看你的了！对比项目崔元俊卢泰文出生年份1970 年1968 年学历斯坦福大学电气工程博士浦项工科大学电气工程博士职业起点科研、无线通信、芯片研发三星手机研发工作背景高通、Atheros、三星长期任职三星加入三星2016 年1997 年核心专长通信技术、芯片、系统整合手机研发、产品规划、商业运营管理风格技术整合、用户需求导向经营效率、规模化导向创新理念解决实际痛点，重视技术落地重视成熟技术的商业化硬件策略未来有待观察相对稳健，重视成本软件理念强调系统级 AI、跨应用协同推动 One UI 生态及 Galaxy AI 折叠屏参与 Fold 系列研发，未来直接领导推动 Fold 系列商业化和普及成本控制尚待观察强调供应链效率最大优势底层技术背景、跨企业研发经验丰富的经营经验、组织管理能力主要挑战证明独立掌舵能力平衡创新、成本和业务规模未来职责直接领导 Galaxy 手机业务统筹 DX 及机器人等未来业务

articles.title: 长安启源 Q06 增推 602 越享+ 版：升级座椅通风加热 + 50W 无线充电，限时权益价 13.59 万元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，长安启源官方今日宣布为 Q06 新增一款“602 越享 +”版车型，官方指导价 13.99 万元，限时权益价仍为 13.59 万元，与原有的 602 越享型持平。新车型的核心变化在于舒适配置的下放，在入门版基础上增配了前排座椅通风加热、50W 手机无线充电以及氛围灯三项功能。602 越享型此前作为全系入门版本，虽然标配了感应后备厢、全车无钥匙进入等实用功能，但在座椅舒适性配置上留有明显空缺。此次“越享 +”的加入，实质上是对入门款配置短板的针对性补齐。启源 Q06 定位中型 SUV，车身长宽高为 4837/1970/1670mm，轴距 2940mm。在动力与三电层面，新车延续了现款 602 版本的基础规格。车辆搭载后置单电机，最大功率 225kW，峰值扭矩 290N·m，零百加速时间 7.1 秒。另外，新车搭载了 66.02kWh 磷酸铁锂电池，CLTC 纯电续航里程 602km，并基于 800V 平台打造，支持 6C 快充。相关阅读：《长安启源 Q06 新增宁德时代电池选装，纯电里程 602 公里》《长安启源 Q06 车型上市：首搭天枢领航高阶智能驾驶辅助，限时权益价 13.59 万元起》

articles.title: 山灵 EH50 台式解码耳放一体机发售：双 CS4308P、6125mW@32Ω 输出功率，首发 1998 元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，山灵 EH50 台式解码耳放一体机于今日正式发布，首发定价为 1998 元，官方零售价 2098 元。京东山灵（SHANLING）EH50 台式解码耳放一体机无损 HIFI 桌面解码耳放数字音频放大器三档增益大推力蓝牙 6.0 支持手机 APP 黑色 1997.5 元直达链接山灵 EH50 搭载两颗 Cirrus Logic 旗舰级八通道 DAC 芯片 CS4308P，组成双芯十六通道解码架构，整机信噪比高达 124dB，失真低至 0.0005%，支持 PCM 768kHz/32bit、DSD512 硬解。耳放电路方面，EH50 延续山灵旗舰模拟电路设计，I/V 转换采用 TI OP1678 低噪声运放搭配 OPA1612 音频专用运放进行低通滤波，耳放部分采用 NE5532 电压放大搭配分立式三极管构成互补推挽电路，架构延续自旗舰 EH90，拥有出色的电流输出能力与动态余量，整体音色趋于暖润厚实。驱动性能上，EH50 配备高、中、低三挡增益调节，4.4mm 平衡输出最高功率达 6125mW@32Ω，3.5mm/6.35mm 单端输出最高 1665mW@32Ω，可驱动高阻抗动圈耳机或低灵敏度平板耳机。接口配置上，EH50 数字输入支持 USB、光纤、同轴以及蓝牙 6.0（支持 LDAC / AAC / SBC），耳机输出配备 3.5mm 单端、6.35mm 单端与 4.4mm 平衡接口，模拟输出提供 RCA 单端与 XLR 平衡输出，支持线路 / 前级输出，可连接有源音箱、功率放大器等设备。供电系统方面，EH50 配备新一代定制 30W 高速率电源，兼顾低噪声、高效率与稳定输出，减少不同电路之间的相互干扰，进一步降低电源噪声对音频信号的影响，为整机运行提供持续可靠的能量支持。功能体验上，EH50 内置 31 段 PEQ 参数均衡功能，支持通过网页端精细调节，也可通过手机 Eddict Player APP 调整增益、滤波、PEQ 等设置，搭配多种预设调音风格，可根据不同耳机特性与个人喜好自由调整听感。外观设计上，EH50 机身采用航空级铝合金打造，经过精密加工与喷砂氧化处理，搭配高强度玻璃面板，提供经典黑、银双色可选；正面搭载 2.2 英寸高清彩色显示屏（120×420），UI 简洁直观，支持旋钮与 APP 操控，机身尺寸为 205×188×53mm（IT之家注：含底座），重量约 1.7kg。 京东 山灵（SHANLING）EH50 台式解码耳放一体机无损 HIFI 桌面解码耳放数字音频放大器三档增益大推力蓝牙 6.0 支持手机 APP 黑色 2350 元 直达链接

articles.title: 国产豪华倒三轮车型 MTPEAK One All 首秀：2.0T + 9AT 动力，首批全球限量 100 台
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，重庆光宇摩托车旗下全新品牌 MTPEAK 本月参加了 2026 米兰车展，带来旗下首款豪华倒三轮车型 MTPEAK One All。这是一款复古造型的倒三轮车型，有点像敞篷老爷车，采用方向盘控制，能坐两个人，形态介于摩托车和汽车之间。根据官方介绍，MTPEAK One All（暂定名）采用中置后驱、前双轮后单轮的运动三轮架构，配备前双叉臂、后边置双减震，以及碳陶通风刹车系统与 305mm 后胎，50:50 均衡配重。全车沿用车规级研发、调校与装配标准，铬钼合金空间架构 + 碳纤维车身覆盖件。动力方面，该车搭载 2.0T 中置涡轮增压发动机 + 9AT 变速箱，最大功率 165kW，峰值扭矩 385N·m，推重比 370 马力 / 吨。MTPEAK One All 首批全球限量 100 台，另有 14 款官方配置可选，包括可拆卸车顶、拨片换挡、防滚架、三点式安全带、激光大灯、车载音响等。IT之家查询公开资料获悉，重庆光宇工业成立于 1996 年，拥有“凯诺牌”“豪诺牌”“豪鹰牌”摩托车；于 2005 年进军汽车零部件领域，2023 年启动 MTPEAK 项目。

articles.title: 国家能源局：截至 10 月底我国电动汽车充电基础设施（枪）总数达 2539.1 万个，同比增长 36.2%
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，11 月 20 日，国家能源局发布 2026 年 10 月全国电动汽车充电设施数据。根据国家充电设施监测服务平台数据，截至 2026 年 10 月底，我国电动汽车充电基础设施（枪）总数达到 2539.1 万个，同比增长 36.2%。IT之家从报告获悉，其中，公共充电设施（枪）528.3 万个，同比增长 16.5%，额定总功率达到 2.71 亿千瓦，单枪平均功率约为 51.37 千瓦；私人充电设施（枪）2010.8 万个，同比增长 42.5%，私人充电设施报装用电容量达到 1.71 亿千伏安。延伸阅读文章提到的充电设施规划目标，源自 2025 年 9 月由国家发展改革委、国家能源局等六部门联合印发的《电动汽车充电设施服务能力“三年倍增”行动方案（2025—2027 年）》。该方案明确，到 2027 年底在全国范围内建成 2800 万个充电设施，提供超 3 亿千瓦的公共充电容量，满足超过 8000 万辆电动汽车充电需求，实现充电服务能力的翻倍增长。从近年数据看，我国电动汽车充电设施总量保持高速增长：截至 2025 年 12 月底突破 2000 万大关，达 2009.2 万个；2026 年 1 月底达 2069.8 万个；2026 年 3 月底达 2148.1 万个；2026 年 8 月底达 2422.3 万个；2026 年 9 月底达 2477.7 万个。充电设施规模快速扩张背后，是新能源汽车保有量的持续攀升。据中国汽车工业协会数据，截至 2026 年 3 月底，全国新能源汽车保有量约 4550 万辆，整体车桩比达到 2.12:1，较 2020 年的 3.5:1 有了明显改善。在规模增长的同时，公共充电桩的单枪功率也在稳步提升。数据显示，截至 2026 年 3 月底，全国公共充电桩额定总功率达到 2.34 亿千瓦，平均功率约 48.06 千瓦，较 2024 年的约 40 千瓦提升了 20% 以上，意味着同样数量的充电桩能够提供更强的充电能力。

articles.title: 三星 One UI 9.5 测试 Days：把通话、出行和支付等串成每日时间线
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，科技媒体 SammyGuru 昨日（11 月 19 日）发布博文，报道称在 One UI 9.5 首个 Beta 测试版中，三星正在测试 Days 功能，尝试将用户一天的活动自动整理成时间线。该媒体指出三星此前曾测试 Memory 功能，主打集中保存截图、链接、笔记和语音备忘录，并借助 AI 添加标签、生成摘要和整理内容。IT之家援引博文介绍，Days 在 Memory 基础上进一步扩展到生活记录，测试设置列出的活动包括通话与短信、到访地点、支付、睡眠与运动，以及音乐、视频、网页浏览等，希望以日记形式串联用户一天的经历。按照曝光的设计，用户可以切换查看每日精选或全部活动，也能跳转至指定日期，并手动补充标题、图片和地点。隐私控制方面，用户可选择记录类别、隐藏单条活动，或停止保存特定来源的信息。访问时间线还需开启三星“个人数据智能”功能。
